GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2014-10-09T14:17:28Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Router: Cannot use literal characters \] and \) in Regex
Description: I know is horrible having special characters in URLs but I sadly have to manage them, so I tried to use this route:

``` javascript
router.get("/thumb/:file([a-zA-Z\-0-9\/ \._\%,&\[\]]+)/:size", function (req, res) {
   //do stuff
});
```

to handle an URL like: `/thumb/canada/news-events/event-list/185-Roma_Ghezzi[1].jpg/75x75`

Adding the character `\\]` will make the route stop working, even if the URL doesn't contain those characters.

Even worst when you try adding the characters `\\(` or `\\)` because it crashes the process with the error:

```
SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: /^\/thumb\/(?:([a-zA-Z-0-9\/ \._%,&[]))]+)\/(?:([^\/]+?))\/?$/: Unmatched ')'
    at new RegExp (<anonymous>)
```

I'd really prefer to use this a rule like the following one:

``` javascript
router.get("/thumb/:file(.+)/:size", function (req, res) {
   //do stuff
});
```

but the expression `(.+)` doesn't match a string like: `folder/subfolder/file` because the slashes `/` are considered a stop character (I guess).

REASONING: This issue is about a regex pattern in Express.js router routes that doesn't properly handle certain special characters like square brackets and parentheses. The problem is purely related to the syntax of regular expressions in JavaScript and how Express.js router interprets them. 

To verify the solution, one would only need to understand:
1. How regex patterns work in JavaScript
2. How Express.js router handles regex patterns in route definitions
3. The proper escaping of special characters in regex patterns

This is a conceptual issue that can be analyzed without building or running the code. The solution would involve proper escaping of special characters in the regex pattern or using a different approach to route definition.
